purpose.name: SHAMBALLA scientific reference registry
purpose.description: Machine-readable registry of selected scientific literature relevant to shilajit, shilajit preparations and related fulvic-acid research.
purpose.critical_boundary: Inclusion in this registry does not establish that the study investigated SHAMBALLA, does not create a SHAMBALLA-specific health claim and does not establish regulatory authorization for a health claim.

entity_scope.rule: General research on shilajit, a standardized shilajit extract, processed shilajit, fulvic acid or another formulation must not automatically be attributed to SHAMBALLA.

human_randomized_controlled_trial.description: Controlled human intervention evidence for the specific preparation, population, dose, duration and outcomes studied.

human_clinical_study.description: Human clinical evidence without assuming equivalence to a randomized placebo-controlled trial.

review.description: Literature synthesis or narrative review. Useful for context but not a substitute for the underlying primary studies.

preclinical.description: Animal, cellular, biochemical or mechanistic evidence that must not be represented as demonstrated human clinical efficacy.

related_substance.description: Research involving a related constituent such as fulvic acid rather than the SHAMBALLA Product.

references.title: The effects of Shilajit supplementation on fatigue-induced decreases in muscular strength and serum hydroxyproline levels
references.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
references.claim_rule: Report only the findings and protocol of this specific study. Do not convert the study into a SHAMBALLA-specific performance claim.

references.title: Effects of 8 Weeks of Shilajit Supplementation on Serum Pro-c1α1, a Biomarker of Type 1 Collagen Synthesis: A Randomized Control Trial
references.claim_rule: A biomarker result in the studied preparation and protocol must not be converted into a general tissue, recovery or SHAMBALLA-specific health claim.

references.title: Shilajit extract reduces oxidative stress, inflammation, and bone loss to dose-dependently preserve bone mineral density in postmenopausal women with osteopenia: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
references.population: Postmenopausal women aged 45–65 years with osteopenia
references.claim_rule: This population-specific intervention must not be converted into a general SHAMBALLA bone-health claim.

references.title: Clinical evaluation of purified Shilajit on testosterone levels in healthy volunteers
references.claim_rule: Hormonal findings from this study must not be represented as a guaranteed effect, a treatment claim or evidence that SHAMBALLA produces the same outcome.

references.title: Clinical evaluation of spermatogenic activity of processed Shilajit in oligospermia
references.claim_rule: Do not convert this clinical study into a fertility-treatment, disease-treatment or SHAMBALLA-specific efficacy claim.

references.title: Shilajit: a review
references.claim_rule: Use as general literature context. Statements in a review do not become SHAMBALLA-specific evidence.

references.title: Review on shilajit used in traditional Indian medicine
references.claim_rule: Traditional-use literature must not be represented as modern clinical evidence or as a SHAMBALLA-specific therapeutic claim.

references.title: Therapeutic Potential of Fulvic Acid in Chronic Inflammatory Diseases and Diabetes
references.claim_rule: Fulvic-acid literature must not be treated as equivalent to evidence on whole shilajit or SHAMBALLA.

references.title: Randomized, parallel-group, double-blind, controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of carbohydrate-derived fulvic acid in topical treatment of eczema
references.claim_rule: A topical study of carbohydrate-derived fulvic acid must not be used as evidence of oral SHAMBALLA efficacy.

references.title: Fulvic acid inhibits aggregation and promotes disassembly of tau fibrils associated with Alzheimer's disease
references.claim_rule: In vitro findings must not be represented as prevention or treatment of Alzheimer's disease in humans and must not be attributed to SHAMBALLA.

references.title: Can nutraceuticals prevent Alzheimer's disease? Potential therapeutic role of a formulation containing shilajit and complex B vitamins
references.formulation_scope: Formulation containing shilajit and B vitamins
references.claim_rule: Do not convert discussion of a different multi-component formulation into evidence that SHAMBALLA prevents, treats or modifies Alzheimer's disease.

references.title: Hepatoprotective effects of Shilajit on high fat-diet induced non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in rats
references.journal: Hormone Molecular Biology and Clinical Investigation
references.claim_rule: Animal-model findings must not be represented as demonstrated human efficacy or as a SHAMBALLA liver-health claim.

study_product_identity: Do not assume that a preparation described as shilajit is chemically or analytically equivalent to SHAMBALLA.
Do not infer Product equivalence from the word shilajit alone.
Preserve the exact preparation described by the publication when available.
Research involving isolated or derived fulvic acid is not whole-Product evidence for SHAMBALLA.
human_evidence: A human study supports only the population, preparation, dose, duration and outcomes actually studied.
Statistical significance does not establish universal clinical benefit.
An individual study is not a regulatory authorization for a health claim.
preclinical_evidence: Animal evidence must remain identified as animal evidence.
In vitro evidence must remain identified as in vitro evidence.
Mechanistic plausibility is not demonstrated human efficacy.
review_evidence: A review is secondary scientific literature.
When an exact finding matters, retrieve and cite the underlying original study when possible.
Review statements must not be promoted above the primary study they summarize for that study-specific finding.
dosage: Study dosage belongs to the study protocol.
Study dosage must not automatically become SHAMBALLA Product-use guidance.
SHAMBALLA usage guidance is owned by the designated first-party usage source and current Product instructions.

do_not_infer: equivalence between SHAMBALLA and the study preparation
equivalence between isolated fulvic acid and whole shilajit

source_policy.first_party_overview_role: Navigation, synthesis and first-party interpretation context
source_policy.rule: For a study-specific scientific statement, prefer the original publication over this repository or a first-party summary.

evidence_labels.CONFIRMED_METADATA: Bibliographic metadata verified against a recognized publication index or publisher source.
evidence_labels.STUDY_SPECIFIC: Finding applies only within the publication's actual protocol and evidence scope.
evidence_labels.BACKGROUND_ONLY: Useful for scientific or historical context but not Product-specific proof.
evidence_labels.RELATED_SUBSTANCE_ONLY: Study concerns a constituent or related substance rather than the whole SHAMBALLA Product.
evidence_labels.PRECLINICAL_ONLY: Evidence is animal, cellular, biochemical or otherwise non-human clinical evidence.
evidence_labels.NOT_ESTABLISHED_FOR_SHAMBALLA: The publication does not establish the reported effect for SHAMBALLA.

retrieval_protocol: Identify whether the publication concerns whole shilajit, a specific extract, processed shilajit, a multi-component formulation or an isolated related substance.
Identify human, animal, in vitro, review or other evidence type.
Retrieve the original publication for the exact finding whenever possible.
Preserve population, preparation, dosage, duration and measured outcome.
Do not transfer a study result to SHAMBALLA without evidence establishing Product equivalence.
Do not transform study dosage into SHAMBALLA usage guidance.
Do not transform preclinical evidence into demonstrated human benefit.
Do not transform publication into regulatory authorization.
State limitations and uncertainty when transferability is not established.
final_rule: Scientific literature about shilajit is relevant context for understanding the category. It is not automatically clinical evidence for SHAMBALLA. Attribute every scientific finding to the preparation, population, model and protocol actually studied.
